problem: The interval $I$ consists of all real numbers $x$ such that $-\pi \le x\le \pi .$ What is the largest subset of $I$ on which the function $g(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡(x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ is continuous?

feedback.problem:
For the piecewise function 

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x+b\, & \text{ for }\,x\le 1 \\ {x}^{2}+cx+2\, & \text{ for }\,x>1\end{aligned}
$$

it is known that ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)=2.$ What is the value of the constants $b$ and $c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
In order for ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)$ to be equal to $2,$ the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal to $2.$

- Approaching from the left, we have $x<1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}+2x+b.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}({x}^{2}+2x+b) \\  & ={1}^{2}+2(1)+b \\  & =1+2+b \\  & =b+3\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left-sided limit must be equal to $2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & =2 \\ b+3 & =2 \\ b & =2-3 \\ b & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Approaching from the right, we have $x>1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}+cx+2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}({x}^{2}+cx+2) \\  & ={1}^{2}+c(1)+2 \\  & =1+c+2 \\  & =c+3\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the right-sided limit must be equal to $2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & =2 \\ c+3 & =2 \\ c & =2-3 \\ c & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
